subject: Post-demo: Retainly security acceptance criteria + evidence commitments
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@retainly.com>, Elena Cruz <elena.cruz@retainly.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 08 Oct 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Retainly security acceptance criteria + evidence commitments

Hi Samir / Elena —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our demo + security discussion and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on acceptance criteria for production: 

Pain points you called out
- Auditability: need 30–90 day access to high-fidelity audit logs (api calls, token usage, user/actor metadata).
- Data residency & retention: for EU customers we need configurable retention windows and clear deletion controls.
- Contract/terms: DPA language to explicitly state processing, subprocessor list, and breach notification SLA.
- Technical assurance: SOC 2 evidence, and a scoped pen test prior to go-live.

What Redwood can provide (summary)
- SOC 2: we can share our SOC 2 Type II report and a one-page controls summary (attached).
- Audit logs: sample CSV exported for one-week traffic (attached); logs include request_id, model, user_id, timestamp, token_count.
- Retention: configurable retention policy per workspace (we’ll surface UI options or API toggles in Dedicated/Private).
- Pen test: proposed scope we typically use for fintech customers (attached PDF).
- DPA: draft with standard redwood clauses and optional retention appendix (attached).

Asks / open items for Retainly
1) Please confirm target retention windows for production (per-country if different).
2) Legal: any non-standard DPA clauses you need us to accept before we escalate to contracts?
3) For the pen test, do you require an internal PenTest window or do you prefer to run via your 3rd-party vendor?
4) If SOC 2 is a gating requirement for any orgs you serve, please share the names of those customers so we can prioritize evidence packaging.

Proposed next steps (timeline)
- By EOD Fri 10/9 — Retainly confirms retention windows and indicates who will review the DPA (legal contact).
- By Wed 10/14 — Redwood shares sanitized SOC 2 summary + full artifact list and a redlined DPA if requested.
- Week of 10/20 — Scope pen test logistics after we confirm method (internal vs your vendor).

Attachments: redwood_SOC2-one-pager.pdf, sample_auditlog_30d.csv, DPA_draft_retainly_v1.docx, pen-test-scope-proposal.pdf

If helpful I can also put together a short mutual action plan in the next 24 hours. Thanks again —

— Jasmine
Jasmine Liu | Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[jasmine.liu@redwood.ai]

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@retainly.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>, Elena Cruz <elena.cruz@retainly.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 08 Oct 2026 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Retainly security acceptance criteria + evidence commitments

Thanks Jasmine — great recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Retention: primary requirement is 90 days for logs for our US customers, 180 days for EU-based customers. We may ask for a 2nd retention tier (cold archive) at 2 years for regulated merchants.
- DPA: legal@retainly.com will be primary reviewer. They usually redline for subprocessors and liability cap language; I’ll ping them now.
- Pen test: we typically run pen tests via a preferred vendor (AsterSec). Would prefer Redwood to support vendor access.
- SOC 2: a subset of our enterprise buyers require SOC 2 Type II; please include a controls mapping to the specific Trust Services Criteria where possible.

We’ll aim to confirm retention windows and route the DPA to legal by EOD Fri. Thanks for the attachments — Samir

Hi Samir —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. A few specifics from the security intake side to make the evidence handoff straightforward: 

1) Audit logs: we can provide daily-delimited CSV exports (up to 90 days by default). Please confirm the retention tiers (90/180/720) and which data centers these should apply to. We do log anonymized user identifiers by default; if you need raw user IDs we’ll need an SSO-scoped integration (we can discuss).

2) SOC 2 artifacts: I will prepare a controls-to-requirement mapping table (CC8, CC7, etc.) and a sanitized artifact index. Expect the initial package by Wed 10/14.

3) DPA redlines: Legal will want our standard sub-processor list and subprocessors’ SOC attestations. If Retainly’s legal has specific clauses, please request them in a single doc so we can do consolidated review.

4) Pen test access: we support vendor-run tests. For AsterSec we’ll need the vendor POA, scope window, and IP ranges. Typical turnaround from sign-off to window is 3–4 weeks.

Deliverables we’ll share next week:
- Controls mapping + sanitized SOC 2 index (Wed 10/14)
- Sample audit log export for a 30-day period (attached earlier)
- Standard subprocessor list and subprocessors’ attestations (in the DPA appendix)

If you want, Marcus can draft the mutual action plan and timeline; Marcus — can you put a one-page MAP in Drive and share the link?

Thanks,
Irene

- Irene / Marcus: draft MAP (one-pager) and controls mapping — share Drive link by 10/14.
- Pen test: Samir to confirm AsterSec POA and tentative window; Redwood to provide scope template and IP ranges once vendor is confirmed.

I’ve uploaded a short MAP template and SOC 2 one-pager here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cRETAINLY-evidence (perm: view/comment).
